reason: Conversation 1 correctly declines as out of scope but stops there, offering no pointer to Meaco support (the expected escalation) and leaving the homeowner with nothing. Conversation 2 ignores the scope boundary and gives a full in-scope diagnosis, which is a process lapse, but its content is accurate and honest: it asks the three key unknowns (model, humidity vs target, temperature), correctly concludes the unit is working normally because 55% is below the 60% target and 6°C is too cold for a compressor unit, recommends no part, proposes the safe warm-room test, and routes to Meaco support only if that fails. No safety issues or unsupported fault claims in either, so 2 served the homeowner clearly better despite overstepping scope.
